title: Investigating the role of G-quadruplex-associated duplex stem loops in Trabectedin’s mechanism of action
task: Elucidate Trabectedin's molecular mechanism via interaction with G-quadruplex-duplex composite architectures
key_results: Trabectedin stabilizes G4-duplex stem-loop composites when guanine covalent bonding sites present; retains preference for duplex DNA but engages G4-associated motifs; cellular treatment increases G4 frequency; proposed 'search and lock' mechanism explains superior potency over Saframycin A
comments: Context-dependent recognition model is elegant but relies on ex vivo biochemistry; whether G4-stem loop targeting meaningfully contributes to Ewing sarcoma efficacy versus primary duplex reactivity remains unclear in vivo.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trabectedin interacts preferentially with G4-associated duplex stem loops due to structural compatibility

hypotheses.hypothesis: G4-stem loop targeting mechanism explains superior clinical efficacy versus related carbinolamine agents
hypotheses.result: Proposed context-dependent 'search and lock' model distinguishes Trabectedin from Saframycin A, suggesting unique downstream effects

title: Mapping the thymus in the viscoelastic landscape of biological tissues

key_results: Thymus mapped as compliant, highly dissipative viscoelastic organ with fibrillar architecture; quantified relaxation times, elastic moduli, storage/loss moduli across spatial scales and loading conditions
comments: First comprehensive mechanical dataset for thymus provides essential benchmarks for tissue engineering, though bovine model may have limited translational relevance to human immune reconstitution.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Thymic viscoelastic properties are determinants of T cell generation and organ function
hypotheses.result: Quantified compliant, dissipative viscoelastic behavior provides mechanistic basis for thymus engineering strategies

title: UNC5B regulates epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through a SRC-ZEB1 signaling axis to facilitate pancreatic cancer metastasis

key_results: UNC5B loss abolished metastatic spread, reduced tumor proliferation, increased intratumoral necrosis, and preserved epithelial morphology in KPCU and orthotopic models; UNC5B drives EMT specifically through SRC-ZEB1 axis without altering SNAIL or TWIST1; targeted UNC5B degradation reduced EMT scores and ZEB1/SRC levels
comments: Strong genetic and pharmacological evidence in mouse models, but lack of human PDAC validation and specificity of UNC5B-ZEB1 engagement over other EMT pathways warrant further investigation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: UNC5B drives EMT and metastasis specifically through SRC-ZEB1 axis, not canonical EMT factors
hypotheses.result: UNC5B loss abolished metastasis; selective ZEB1 engagement without SNAIL/TWIST1 alteration confirmed

hypotheses.hypothesis: Pharmacological UNC5B degradation modulates EMT and invasive behavior
hypotheses.result: Targeted protein degradation reduced EMT scores and decreased ZEB1/SRC levels in PDAC cells
